Hello! My name is Maggie and I work for a startup that operates several websites. We post to these websites very frequently and are looking to develop automations to make the process of publishing articles more streamlined and efficient. Our website is built on react and next.js.

- About the project - 
We would like to build a program to generate JSON schema. On every page we publish, we need article, breadcrumb, and organization schema. On pages that have FAQs and videos, we need schema for those.

Second, a program I can run locally that will parse each page, collect the information necessary for the component, and insert it.

jobs.title: Shopify development: Two prices on product page and in checkout (Price & Compare Price)
jobs.description:
Shopify expert in custom code and functions.

Briefly about the concept: We build many e-coms which are membership clubs. It is also possible to shop at higher prices without membership. The task is that we have to build in Shopify so that visitors can choose for themselves whether they want to shop at member price or normal price. If people choose membership price, we have to include a specific parameter, so that we know in our other systems that this customer must have a membership (the last part is not part of the first task here).

This means that we must have built in Shopify so that a customer can shop at two different prices. We must have two buttons on each product page (see attached design with two buttons and two different prices).

The one "add to basket" button is to add a product to the basket at member price. We will use the "Price" field in Shopify for this one.

The second "add to basket" button is to add the product to the basket at the normal price. We need to use the "Compare Price" price field in Shopify for this one.

The last product price selection, which is placed in the basket, must determine whether the entire order must be at member price or normal price.

The total price at checkout must be either the member-only price (Price) or the normal price (Compare Price) depending on the customer's choice.

UI design is not part of the task at the start, but may be afterwards. The most important thing is that we get the function done, so to start with, you can just insert two different add to basket buttons to test the function.

Is this something you have the skills to build - and if so, how quickly would you be able to build this?

There will be a number of other tasks in the future as well, but it is important that we solve this one first to see how the collaboration will progress.

jobs.title: Sampling analog signal
jobs.description:
Sampling an analog signal is a crucial step for any digital signal processing system. The Nyquist–Shannon
sampling theorem guarantees a full recovery of the signal when sampling with a frequency larger than or equal to the
bandwidth of the signal (or double the maximum frequency in case of real signals).


Description: Develop a web application that illustrates the signal sampling and recovery showing the importance and
validation of the Nyquist rate. You application should have the following features:

- Sample & Recover: Allow the user to load a mid-length signal (around 1000 points length), visualize and sample
it via different frequencies, then use the sampled points to recover the original signal using Whittaker–Shannon
interpolation formula (please, refer to this wiki page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nyquist%E2%80%93Shannon_sampling_theorem) for more information). Sampling frequency should be
shown in either actual frequency or normalized one (with respect to the maximum frequency, i.e. ranges from
0×fmax to 4×fmax for example). You should use three graphs, one for displaying the original signal along with the
markers for the sampled points and another one to display the reconstructed signal, and lastly the third one
should display the difference between the original signal and the reconstructed one.

- Load & Compose: The loaded signal can come a file or a signal mixer/composer in your application. In the signal
mixer, the user can add multiple sinusoidal signals of different frequencies and magnitudes. The user can also
remove any of the components during preparing the mixed signal.

- Additive noise: The user can add noise to the loaded signal with custom/controllable SNR level. The program
should be able to show the dependency of the noise effect on the signal frequency.

- Real-time: Sampling and recovery should be done in real time upon user changes (i.e. no button called “update”
or “Refresh” is allowed).

- Resize: The application can be resized easily without messing up your UI.

- Different sampling scenarios: In your submission, you need to prepare at least 3 testing synthetic signals
(generated and saved through your Composer) that address different testing scenarios. One example test case is the one mentioned below:
o A mix (i.e. summation) of 2Hz and 6Hz sinusoidals. If sampled with 12Hz or above, then it should be
recovered nicely. But if sampled with 4Hz, then the two frequencies will show up as just one frequency.
What if the signal is sampled with 8Hz?

Provide 3 more samples; each would exploit a problem or illustrate a tricky feature.

jobs.title: Two Hours of Training on openHAB and Using Webhooks from WordPress to Control Alexa Devices
jobs.description:
We are looking for an openHAB expert to prepare and deliver two hours of training on how to integrate an external website (on WordPress) to openHAB using webhooks or API in order to pass text commands to Alexa devices and check for status (e.g., on, off, etc.) of devices.  The goal is to train a small number of business users (with entry-level programming skills in JavaScript and PHP) on how they can utilize webhooks and/or API calls to openHAB to control smart devices attached to Amazon's Alexa and to update the WordPress website with the status of devices. NO WordPress training is needed; participants will already know how to send and receive webhooks or API calls from/ to WordPress.

By the conclusion of the training, attendees will have:
1)	Learned the basics of openHAB, its models and components (bindings, things, channels, items, rules, and scripts)
2)	Learned how to trigger Alexa TextCommands by sending a webhook or API request to openHAB from a WordPress site
3)	Learned how to return to the WordPress site status information for Alexa-connected devices from openHAB
4)	Sent their first TextCommand request to Alexa
5)	Polled (send inquiry to) openHAB for status information of one Alexa-connected device

The course can be divided into two 1-hr sessions if desired, or delivered as a single 2-hr session.  The training must be delivered live, in English, via teleconference (Zoom, Google Meet, etc.).  Participants will attend from the Eastern time zone of the US.  The sessions should be instructor led with Q&A all throughout.  Prior reading or videos (e.g., YouTube tutorials, sections from the openHAB documentation, etc.) can be assigned for participants to review prior to the training. The live sessions will be recorded ONLY by us the client, will be owned by us the client, and may not be shared with any outside parties as the business content is CONFIDENTIAL.

jobs.title: Construction cost calculator app
jobs.description:
INTRODUCTION
The main goal is to create an application that allows a user to easily calculate the cost of construction of their new house by specifying which rooms and spaces will be in the house.

DESCRIPTION
This website/webpage needs to be something where the clients can customize what type of spaces they want in their house and get an estimate of their building cost as well as a Schedule of Accommodation. For example, they should be able to customize how many bedrooms and bathrooms they want in their house and choose any other spaces they might need in it. They should also be able to choose whether their house will be a basic, standard or luxury type.

Whatever they choose will have its own minimum area that will be totalled up to give the building cost estimate. 

Once this is done, there should be an option where the client can choose what services they want us to provide, i.e. architectural drawings, structural drawings, MEP drawings and BOQs. After they decide on what they want, they can place an order, pay a fee and get an invoice from us.

This webpage should be country specific yet changeable; meaning the client must be able to change to any other country they want the design to be in and choose any currency they prefer.

Ensure that you set the prune option properly to reduce disk space requirements. See also here https://prunednode.today to avoid a lengthy process but do not use this blockchain for genuine transactions
Gain some experience with the system and start using the command-line helper bitcoin-cli. For instance,
bitcoin-cli getinfo 
dispays information about the network node. 
bitcoin-cli getblockhash 5000
returns the block hash of block 5000
You can input the block hash above to 
bitcoin-cli getblock 
to get info about the block, including the block header and the transactions. 
Use this info to write a program that returns useful statistical data about some of the parameters in the block header. Using Python, see the python-bitcoinlib library. 
In particular, answer these questions:
- What was the trend of the difficulty parameter this year (2023)? (show either a table or a plot)
- Collect all the Merkle tree roots of the blocks posted this year (2023) and build a Merkle tree of all these values. Release then its root value.
Provide your programs and the answers to the questions above.

jobs.title: Access database - easy SQL querry
jobs.description:
I would like someone to do the following work to the data in an acess table as soon as possible (I know as always!!). Please use SQL querries so that I can see the actual queeries used when the database come back to me. Thank you.

The first SQL querry is as follows:

In the column Q there is a 'x' to indicate it is a row that needs to be divided into 3 ie:

1. from the left hand side to the first coma (,) goes into the surname column;
2. working backwards from the extreme right hand side to the opening bracket (ie ( ) goes into the allelse column;
3. everything from the coma (the coma after the surname) to the opening bracket goes into the initials column.

The second SQL querry is to do the following. There will be some rows with names that have 'x' in the Q column that were not processed. This is because they do not contain an opening bracket. Most of these rows are simply like 'WOOD, C L The 1914-8 War.' For these:

1. from the left hand side to the first coma (,) goes into the surname column;
2. working backwards from the extreme right hand side extract ' The 1914-8 War.' to go into the allelse column;
3. everything from the coma (the coma after the surname) to ' The 1914-8 War.' goes into the initials column.

That is it - if there is anything left over I hope I can deal with it manually.

I have no idea what this is worth in terms of a fee but I did one of these with a techie the other day and it took about 30 minutes. So please sharpen you pencils and bid what it is worth to you.

The full database will be sent to the winning freelancer via dropbox.

Many thanks

jobs.description: Our purpose at the Principals Fund is to build financial sustainable schools in South Africa. A push function to send a subset of this data, grouped by invoice nature/item code/overdue status to the relevant location to be picked up by the credit bureau.4. A login portal for the school team to see the information that has been loaded and sent across to the credit bureau, should queries arise from the relevant parents which the school team can resolve.As the parents are often low income parents, low data usage of either the app or the website is absolutely crucial.At some stage we would seek to have the app loaded onto the Xero/Quickbooks/Sage app store to assist in downloads.Our primary goal is to have a streamlined transfer of information from multiple schools into a single database, which can be fed into the credit bureau in a controlled and auditable way, and which results in little to no extra work from either the parents or the school teams.Budget: $7,500Posted On: February 22, 2024 14:41 UTCCategory: AccountingSkills:Intuit QuickBooks,     API,     API Integration,     Xero,     Sage,     PythonSkills:        Intuit QuickBooks,                     API,                     API Integration,                     Xero,                     Sage,                     PythonCountry: South Africaclick to apply
